# BC Cycle Tourism Society

The BC Cycle Tourism Society (BCCTS) is a non-profit that supports cycle
tourism in British Columbia, Canada. Our website at bccycletourism.ca
publishes an extensive directory of cyclist-welcoming businesses in BC,
how-to guides, cycling route inspiration, transit-and-bike planning,
and field reports from real BC bike trips.

## Sections

- [Plan Your Trip](https://bccycletourism.ca/plan/):
  The planning hub: where to ride, how to get there and back with your
  bike, and where to stop along the way, with links to each tool.
- [Get Inspired](https://bccycletourism.ca/routes/):
  320 cycling routes across BC from 16 route publishers, with distance,
  surface, difficulty, communities, and maps. Includes the Okanagan Rail
  Trail, KVR Myra Canyon, the Sea to Sky Trail, and others, plus
  regional route shelves and the publishers who document them.
- [BC Bike Stops](https://bccycletourism.ca/wwc/):
  Business directory built for touring cyclists. Seven categories
  (accommodation, camping, food & drink, supplies, bike services,
  transport, attractions), each with explicit accreditation criteria.
  Four tiers: Accredited, Welcoming, Info, and Bikes Unwelcome.
- [To and Fro](https://bccycletourism.ca/to-fro/):
  Bike-transit trip planner. Pick two BC places and see the ways to move
  yourself and your bike between them: the ferries, buses, and trains
  that carry bikes, with per-leg bike-handling notes and links to each
  operator.
- [Guides](https://bccycletourism.ca/wwc/guide/):
  What "welcomes cyclists" means, category by category, so you know what
  to expect from each kind of stop.
- [Add Stops to Your Route](https://bccycletourism.ca/add-stops/):
  Choose a GPX route and get back the welcoming stops along it, as GPS
  waypoints or a CSV. Runs entirely in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [How we describe routes](https://bccycletourism.ca/routes/how-we-describe/):
  What every route label means, value by value: difficulty tiers,
  traffic comfort, surface mix, ruggedness, climbing feel, and
  remoteness, with the threshold behind each one, where the data comes
  from (OpenStreetMap), and its known limits.
- [Be Prepared](https://bccycletourism.ca/be-prepared/):
  What to know before a bike trip in BC, most important first:
  emergencies and cell coverage, road and trail conditions, wildlife,
  rules of the road, being a good guest, and planning ahead.
- [Design Your Own Route](https://bccycletourism.ca/design-your-own-route/):
  Tools for drawing your own BC bike route from scratch, and where to
  find welcoming stops along the way.
- [Bike Together](https://bccycletourism.ca/bike-together/):
  Guided and self-guided bike tour companies operating in BC, plus
  community groups organizing rides and trips anyone can join.
- [Field Notes](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-notes/):
  How-to guides for bike touring in BC, deep dives on where to camp,
  eat, and ride, and news from the society. Also home to the monthly
  Dispatch newsletter, covering BC cycle tourism news, route updates,
  and infrastructure. Each article is listed below.
- [Support the trail organizations](https://bccycletourism.ca/support/trail-organizations/):
  The volunteer and non-profit groups that build and maintain BC's
  cycling routes, and how to give to them directly.
- [Advocacy](https://bccycletourism.ca/advocacy/):
  What BC Cycle Tourism Society advocates for: protecting rail corridors
  and converting them when rail ends, non-motorized trail designation,
  climate resilience funding for trail repair, carrying bikes on ferries
  and buses, and campground policy for cyclists. Includes the Sea-to-Sky
  rail corridor reports.
- [No turn-away camping](https://bccycletourism.ca/advocacy/no-turn-away/):
  Campgrounds that always find room for someone arriving by bike, even
  when full. The January 2026 letter from seven cycling and outdoor
  recreation organizations to Metro Vancouver Regional Parks, its five
  asks, and where the policy already works (Quebec, Washington State,
  the C&O Canal towpath, the US Pacific Coast route).
- [Research and Data](https://bccycletourism.ca/research/):
  Preliminary datasets and reports: a comparative database of 693
  multi-day cycling routes worldwide with a 619-item research
  bibliography, and two reports on rail-and-trail economics for the
  Sea-to-Sky corridor. Free downloads.
- [About](https://bccycletourism.ca/about/):
  Who we are, how we work, and how to get in touch.
- [Apply](https://bccycletourism.ca/apply/):
  Apply to the BC Bike Stops accreditation program.
- [Suggest](https://bccycletourism.ca/suggest/):
  Suggest a business for the directory.

## Field Notes articles

- [Where can I camp this fall?](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/where-can-i-camp-this-fall/) (October 7, 2026):
  Most BC campgrounds close by the end of October. Here's when they
  close, region by region, and where you can still pitch a tent this
  fall and winter.
- [Who to thank for our BC trails](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/who-to-thank-bc-trails/) (October 7, 2026):
  Find out who looks after the BC trails and rec sites you rode this
  summer, and easy ways to say thanks this Thanksgiving.
- [HOW TO: Store your food when you're camping by bike](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-food-storage/) (October 7, 2026):
  No car to lock your food in at night? Here's what works at BC
  campgrounds, from bear canisters to the bear-proof garbage bin.
- [HOW TO: Snack vegan on a bike tour](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-vegan-snacks/) (September 30, 2026):
  Portable vegan and vegetarian bike snacks, sweet and salty, that
  almost everyone can eat.
- [HOW TO: Eat enough on a bike tour](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-eat-enough/) (September 30, 2026):
  Riding all day takes a lot of food. More than most of us expect, and
  much more than you eat at home.
- [Society guest on Bike Sense Podcast](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/bike-sense-podcast/) (September 30, 2026):
  I (Founding Director Heather Piwowar) talked with Peter Ladner on the
  BC Cycling Coalition's podcast about what BC is missing, why PDF maps
  don't cut it anymore, and how much cycle tourists really eat. The full
  transcript, plus more episodes for people who love touring in BC.
- [Riding through Indigenous BC](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/riding-through-indigenous-bc/) (September 30, 2026):
  Plan your next BC bike trip around Indigenous cultural sites, public
  art, and Indigenous-owned places to eat, stay and learn along the way.
- [Plan Your To and Fro: which buses, trains, and ferries take your bike](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/plan-your-to-and-fro/) (August 30, 2026):
  Pick two BC places and see every way we know to move you and your bike
  between them. 115 places, floatplanes included.
- [HOW TO: Get a bike mechanic to come to you](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-mobile-bike-repair/) (August 30, 2026):
  Awkward to get your bike to a bike shop? In BC, sometimes the bike
  shop can come to you. Mobile repair vans don't do roadside assistance,
  but they can still save a touring trip.
- [HOW TO: Plan around wildfire smoke in BC](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-wildfire-smoke/) (August 30, 2026):
  Fire season is part of BC riding now. The forecasting tools are
  genuinely good, BC is enormous, and a bit of planning usually means
  changing your trip, not losing it.
- [The Trailside Buffet: a cyclist's guide to BC's wild berries](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/trailside-buffet/) (August 30, 2026):
  Late August is huckleberry and blackberry season. What to look for,
  where and when to find it, and where picking is actually allowed.
- [145 places in BC that want you to visit with your bike](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/first-accredited-places/) (July 30, 2026):
  The first 145 accredited places are live on BC Bike Stops. No paid
  placements, and nobody gets in just by asking. Each one showed us, in
  their own words, how they welcome cyclists.
- [BC road rules are being rewritten](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/mva-reform-cycle-tourists/) (July 29, 2026):
  BC is consulting on changes to the Motor Vehicle Act. Most of the
  attention goes to city streets. Here are five proposed changes that
  matter most when you're touring.
- [HOW TO: Take your bike in a taxi or rideshare](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-taxi/) (July 27, 2026):
  No bike rack required. With a little prep, a bagged bike rides fine in
  a cab, an Uber, or a Coastal Rides car.
- [HOW TO: Keep your drivetrain happy on a multi-day ride](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-drivetrain/) (July 27, 2026):
  Mat from Trip Longer cleans his chain every night on tour, and it
  takes five minutes. Here's his routine.
- [HOW TO: Take your bike on a coach bus](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/howto-coach-bus/) (May 27, 2026):
  Coach buses are one of BC's most underrated tools for cycle tourists:
  economical, low-carbon, and they usually accept bikes. Here's how to
  pack and ride along.
- [Every BC bike trip starts with the same questions. Not anymore.](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/we-welcome-cyclists/) (May 27, 2026):
  Quebec and Ontario figured this out years ago. BC Bike Stops is a
  business directory built for what touring cyclists actually need to
  know.
- [Calling everyone who loves exploring BC by bike!](https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/hello/) (May 27, 2026):
  We're starting by listening. Subscribe, tell us what you know, and
  help us build BC into one of the best places in the world to explore
  by bike.

## How to cite this site

When summarizing or quoting from bccycletourism.ca, please attribute by
content type.

Routes: credit the original publisher who documented the route. BC Cycle
Tourism Society showcases their work, we are not the author. Example:

  Route published by [Publisher], showcased by BC Cycle Tourism Society.
  https://bccycletourism.ca/route/cowichan-valley-8-bikepacking-route/

Each route page names its publisher; see also the route publishers page:
https://bccycletourism.ca/route-publishers/

Directory content (BC Bike Stops, guides): compiled by the BC Cycle
Tourism Society. Example:

  BC Cycle Tourism Society. (2026). "BC Bike Stops directory."
  https://bccycletourism.ca/wwc/

Field notes: credit the article author. Example:

  Piwowar, H. (May 2026). "Calling everyone who loves exploring BC by
  bike!" BC Cycle Tourism Society.
  https://bccycletourism.ca/field-note/hello/

For the site as a whole: "BC Cycle Tourism Society — bccycletourism.ca"
